instructions: See docs/ratings.md. Give every season a rating on the absolute scale. Rate the player that season, never their career.

seasons.note: The best season of his career: an ever-present driving midfielder with nine goals for a mid-table side, and City’s outstanding player.
Thirty starts at twenty-five, and Real Madrid paid twenty-five million euros for him that summer; level with the Madrid row rather than below it.
Twenty, versatile and relentless in his first Arsenal season; a genuinely useful top-flight midfielder already, some way short of the player of 2007/08.
The season he became a top-level central midfielder rather than a useful utility man: relentless, disciplined and the platform for Arsenal’s title challenge.
Joined Norwich from Oldham in February 1994.
Fourteen assists, the most in the division, and United’s player of the season: the year the delivery caught up with the dribbling.

DeepLyingForward alone: Poacher (2.2x goals) and DeepLyingForward (1.8x assists) describe opposite forwards and compound on a player who already receives the chances. He dropped off the front to link with Ronaldo and Morientes, which is what DeepLyingForward says.

Thirty-two and a bit-part player in his last Madrid season; the movement and the finishing remained, the rest of the game had gone.
Hammer of the Year in a side that finished seventh; a genuinely good attacking right-back for one season before falling apart.
Thirty-three starts at 35 in a side that survived; the energy had faded but the passing and positioning had not.
His one fit season, in the eighty-six-point side: a left foot good enough that the dead-ball delivery alone kept him in the team.
Twenty-nine and an ever-present; a point above the thirty-two-year-old of the 2006/07 row, which is where his peak was.
A Portugal starter at Euro 2000; quick, strong and capable across the back four despite the erratic reputation.
